title.back: AI at work: jobs that change
title.note: "Untung atau rugi" (profit or loss, gain or lose) is used for gain/lose throughout the lesson; it is everyday Indonesian, but it can sound like money only. Alternative: "diuntungkan atau dirugikan".

essentialQuestion.source: How might AI change people's jobs, and who gains or loses?
essentialQuestion.back: How can AI change people's jobs, and who gains or loses?

learningGoal.source: Use examples from history to explain how new machines change work, and describe who might gain or lose as AI changes jobs.
learningGoal.back: Use examples from history to explain how new machines change work, and explain who might gain or lose when AI changes jobs.

read.sections.0.heading.source: New machines have changed work before
read.sections.0.heading.back: New machines have changed work before

read.sections.0.text.source: AI is not the first technology to change people's work. In England in the early 1800s, new machines in factories began to do work that skilled cloth workers had done by hand. Between 1811 and 1816, some of these workers, called Luddites, broke machines in protest. The machines were taking their work. Much later, from the 1970s, cash machines slowly spread to banks in the United States. Many people expected bank tellers, who handle money at the counter, to disappear. But a study from 2015 found that the number of tellers stayed about the same and even grew a little. Banks opened more branches, and tellers spent more time helping customers. That was one machine, long ago, so it can't tell us what AI will do.
read.sections.0.text.back: AI is not the first technology that changed people's work. In England in the early 1800s, new machines in factories began to do the work that skilled cloth workers used to do by hand. Between 1811 and 1816, some of these workers, called the Luddites, broke machines as a form of protest. The machines took their work. Long after that, from the 1970s, ATMs slowly spread to banks in the United States. Many people thought bank tellers, the staff who handle money at the counter, would disappear. But a study from 2015 found that the number of tellers stayed more or less the same, and even grew a little. Banks opened more branches, and tellers used more time to help customers. That was only one machine, and very long ago, so that example can't tell us what AI will do.
read.sections.0.text.note: "Cash machines" became "mesin ATM", the everyday word. "Bank tellers" kept as "teller bank" (common in Indonesia), explained in the same sentence. "Luddites" became "kaum Luddite" (the Luddites as a group), the usual Indonesian form; the checker warns that the English plural "Luddites" does not appear.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: AI is not the first technology to change work. In the 1800s, new machines in England did the work of skilled cloth workers. Workers called Luddites broke some machines. From the 1970s, banks in the United States got cash machines. Many thought bank workers at the counter would disappear. A 2015 study found there were still about as many. Banks opened more branches, and workers helped customers more. That was long ago. It can't tell us what AI will do.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: AI is not the first technology that changed work. In the 1800s, new machines in England did the work of skilled cloth workers. Workers called the Luddites broke some machines. From the 1970s, banks in the United States had ATMs. Many people thought bank staff at the counter would disappear. A 2015 study found their number stayed more or less the same. Banks opened more branches, and staff helped customers more. That was long ago. That example can't tell us what AI will do.

read.sections.1.heading.back: AI changes the tasks inside jobs

read.sections.1.text.source: Most jobs are made of many tasks. A new technology may automate some tasks, but not the whole job. When spreadsheets came to office computers in the United States, many bookkeepers lost their work. Yet the number of accountants grew. In 2025, the ILO, the United Nations agency for work, found that about one in four jobs in the world has some exposure to AI tools that write and make things. This means these tools could do some of the tasks in those jobs. It is not a count of jobs lost. Office jobs, such as clerks, have the most exposure. The ILO says most of these jobs are more likely to change than to disappear.
read.sections.1.text.back: Most jobs are made of many tasks. A new technology can automate some tasks, but not the whole job. When spreadsheets began to be used on office computers in the United States, many bookkeepers lost their jobs. However, the number of accountants actually grew. In 2025, the ILO, the UN body that deals with work, found that about one in four jobs in the world is exposed to some degree to AI tools that can write and make things. This means these tools could do some of the tasks in those jobs. This is not a count of jobs lost. Office jobs, such as administrative staff, are the most exposed. According to the ILO, most of these jobs are more likely to change than to disappear.
read.sections.1.text.note: "Has some exposure to" became "sedikit banyak terpapar" (is exposed to some degree). "Spreadsheet" kept, as Indonesian offices say it; "bookkeepers" is "pemegang buku". "AI tools that write and make things" kept as a description rather than "AI generatif", as the English does.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: A job is made of many tasks. A new technology may automate some tasks, not the whole job. Spreadsheets did sums for office workers. Some people who added up numbers lost their work. But there were more accountants. In 2025, a United Nations group studied AI that writes and makes things. About one in four jobs has some exposure to it. It could do some of their tasks. This is not a count of lost jobs. Office jobs have the most exposure. Most will likely change, not disappear.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: One job is made of many tasks. A new technology can automate some tasks, not the whole job. Spreadsheets counted numbers for office workers. Some people whose task was counting numbers lost their jobs. But the number of accountants grew. In 2025, a UN body studied AI that can write and make things. About one in four jobs is exposed to some degree to this AI. This AI could do some of their tasks. This is not a count of jobs lost. Office jobs are the most exposed. Most will probably change, not disappear.

read.sections.2.heading.source: Some people gain, and some people lose

read.sections.2.text.source: Change at work is often uneven. In 2024, the International Monetary Fund warned that AI could help some workers do more, and take important tasks from others. It also said AI will probably make inequality worse unless governments act. In Millbrook, the water office works faster. Two clerks moved to the help desk after training, but one lost her work. Training and fair rules can help. Workers, employers and governments can decide together how new tools are used.
read.sections.2.text.back: Change at work is often uneven. In 2024, the IMF (International Monetary Fund) warned that AI could help some workers produce more, and take important tasks from other workers. The IMF also said that AI will most likely make inequality worse, unless governments act. In Millbrook, the water office now works faster. Two administrative staff moved to the help counter after taking training, but one person lost her job. Training and fair rules can help. Workers, employers and governments can decide together how new tools are used.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: In 2024, money experts said AI may help some workers. It may take big tasks from others. It may make inequality worse, unless leaders act. After training, two Millbrook clerks moved to the help desk. One lost her work. Training and fair rules can help. Workers and leaders can decide together how to use AI.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: In 2024, finance experts said AI might help some workers. AI might take important tasks from other workers. AI might make inequality worse, unless leaders act. After training, two staff in Millbrook moved to the help counter. One person lost her job. Training and fair rules can help. Workers and leaders can decide together how to use AI.
read.sections.2.simpler.note: "Money experts" (the IMF) became "para ahli keuangan" (finance experts).

watch.summary.source: This video asks if machines and AI will take away people's jobs. People have worried about this many times before. In the United States, machines replaced many workers in the 1920s and 1930s. It happened again around 1960. Machines took work on farms, in factories and on telephone lines. But most people still found work. Technology makes some new jobs, such as building and fixing machines. It also makes things cheaper. Then people spend money on other things, like haircuts or eating out, and those need workers too. Some experts say AI is different, because it can do many kinds of work. The video says the bigger question may be who gains. The gains from technology have not been shared fairly. The rules people choose can change that.
watch.summary.back: This video asks whether machines and AI will take people's jobs. People have often worried about this before. In the United States, machines replaced many workers in the 1920s and 1930s. It happened again around 1960. Machines took work in farming, in factories and in telephone networks. But most people still got work. Technology creates some new jobs, like making and fixing machines. Technology also makes goods cheaper. Then people spend their money on other things, like haircuts or eating out, and all of those need workers too. Some experts say AI is different, because AI can do many kinds of work. The video says the bigger question may be who gains. The gains from technology have not been shared fairly. The rules humans choose can change that.

educatorNotes.0.source: One exposure figure in learner text, on purpose. The ILO's (May 2025, with Poland's NASK) is potential exposure to generative AI: 25% of the world's jobs are in occupations where these tools could do some tasks. It is not a count of jobs lost, and the ILO expects most to be transformed rather than replaced; clerical jobs are the most exposed, and in rich countries the jobs most at risk of automation are 9.6% of women's jobs against 3.5% of men's. The IMF's figure (January 2024) has a wider scope: almost 40% of the world's jobs, and about 60% in advanced economies, are exposed to AI in general, with roughly half of those likely to gain and half to see lower demand. Learner text keeps only the IMF's warning about inequality, without its numbers, so the two estimates aren't mixed up. The bank teller example is US data from the 1970s to the 2000s (James Bessen, 2015); it shows one past case, not a forecast for AI. The spreadsheet example is from NPR (2015).
educatorNotes.0.back: Learner text deliberately has only one exposure figure. The ILO's figure (May 2025, with NASK of Poland) is possible exposure to generative AI: 25% of the world's jobs are in kinds of work where some tasks could be done by these tools. It is not a count of jobs lost, and the ILO expects most to change, not be replaced; administrative work is the most exposed, and in rich countries the jobs most at risk of being automated are 9.6% of women's jobs compared with 3.5% of men's. The IMF's figure (January 2024) has a wider scope: almost 40% of the world's jobs, and about 60% in advanced countries, are exposed to AI in general; roughly half may benefit and half may be less needed.
